# Read in coordinate file of PolIII loci atac seq counts
want samples where POL III loci that are 5ppp==1 have high ATAC-seq counts, meaning they are both recognized by RIG-I and have open chromatin allowing POL III transcription
```{r}
pol3_loci_atac_counts <- read.table("~/ron_TCGA_ATAC_pol3_filtered.tsv",
                        header = TRUE,
                        sep = "\t",
                        stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

View(pol3_loci_atac_counts)
pol3_loci_atac_counts %>% select(c(1:10, "identifier", "is_5ppp")) %>% View


# How many RIG-I recognized loci do we have? ####
pol3_loci_atac_counts %>% count(is_5ppp)
#   is_5ppp    n
# 1       0 9502
# 2       1  132

# convert to long format
pol3_loci_atac_counts_long <- pol3_loci_atac_counts %>% 
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("TCGA"),
    names_to = "sample",
    values_to = "counts"
  ) %>% 
  mutate(
    cancer_type = str_extract(sample, "(?<=TCGA\\.)[A-Z]+"),
    counts = as.numeric(counts),
    sample = str_remove(sample, "^TCGA\\.")
  ) 

# filter to the is_5ppp ==1 loci only. want to find 
engager_loci_counts_wide <- pol3_loci_atac_counts_long %>% 
  filter(is_5ppp==1) %>% 
  mutate(locus_id = paste(chr, start, end, sep = "_")) %>% 
  select(sample, cancer_type, locus_id, counts) %>% 
  pivot_wider(names_from = locus_id, values_from = counts)

dim(engager_loci_counts_wide)
# [1] 410 134 -- 410 samples and 134 columns (132 locus columns plus sample and cancer_type)

# Log normalize atac seq counts
engager_loci_counts_log2 <- engager_loci_counts_wide %>% 
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~log2(. +1)))

gmm_fit <- engager_loci_counts_log2 %>% 
  select(-sample, -cancer_type) %>% 
  Mclust()

summary(gmm_fit)

# ---------------------------------------------------- 
# Gaussian finite mixture model fitted by EM algorithm 
# ---------------------------------------------------- 
# 
# Mclust EEI (diagonal, equal volume and shape) model with 9 components: 
# 
#  log-likelihood   n   df     BIC       ICL
#       -63058.78 410 1328 -134107 -134111.4
# 
# Clustering table:
#   1   2   3   4   5   6   7   8   9 
#  91 167   8   4   1   1  45   1  92 

```
